rationale: This is a cosmetic denominator tweak to the archived "Prior-Capex Cash Payoff" (LAG(capx+dp,1) instead of MA(LAG(capx,1),3)) with the identical mechanism, expected sign, and numerator, so it cannot diagnose why that signal's cross-sectional and portfolio evidence was only marginal.

Replacing the archived Inventory Margin Divergence's margin *trend* with the margin *level* both re-treads that already-tested interaction and injects a direct rediscovery of the gross-profitability anomaly (IND_RANK(cogs/sale) is inverse gross margin), so any result will be hard to attribute to the inventory-quality mechanism.

The negative absolute rank-distance construction is genuinely distinct from the archive and from level-based investment/profitability anomalies, and the hypothesis matches the expression's direction, though the short leg deliberately pools over- and under-investors whose returns may partially offset — a diagnosis worth tracking if the spread is weak.

Multiplying by INDICATOR(NEG(oancf),0) zeroes the large majority of firms, leaving a degenerate cross-section (huge point mass at zero plus a distressed tail) whose predictive content is essentially the well-documented negative-cash-flow/financial-distress effect rather than a novel "runway" interaction.

The lagged-capacity-build conditioning on a signed gross-margin change is internally consistent and economically distinct from the archive's contemporaneous inventory–margin combinations, but the signal is largely a change-in-profitability measure with a mass of non-builders at zero, so the effective sort spans only part of the cross-section.

Structurally near-identical to Post-Build Margin Erosion (signed profitability change × investment indicator) with the same zero-mass issue, and its likely drivers — change in cash ROA plus acquisition-driven intangible growth — overlap heavily with published profitability-change and post-merger underperformance anomalies while intan's sparse reporting will further thin coverage.
